_comment: Copy to forward_levels.json and fill in. That filename is gitignored, so
licensed forward assessments stay out of this public repository.
Anything you omit falls back to the hardcoded assumptions in run_model.py.
currency  — applies to the interconnector levels only. EUR (default) is
converted at the ECB daily reference rate; GBP is used as-is.
NBP and UK ETS are always GBP.
levels    — BASELOAD forward per link for the forecast window, not peak:
the model applies an intraday shape from ENTSO-E on top, so a
peak assessment would count the daily shape twice. Omit a link
or set null to use the trailing ENTSO-E realised mean instead.
nbp_p_therm — either a single number for the whole window, or the daily
curve shown below. A curve is preferred: NBP moves day to day
and gas sets the GB price in most periods, so this is the
single most sensitive input in the model (about 0.62 GBP/MWh
per p/therm at the marginal 55% tranche). Dates outside the
modelled window are ignored; gaps inside it hold the nearest
quoted day. No intraday shape: a gas day is one product, so a
plant's fuel cost is flat across all 48 settlement periods.
uk_ets_gbp_tonne — one number. Carbon is an annual compliance instrument,
so it takes neither an intraday nor a daily shape. CPS is a
frozen statutory rate and stays in run_model.py.
All values below are placeholders, not assessments.
